proposed_comments.title: Select the custom WPR profile explicitly
proposed_comments.body:
## [P2] Select the custom WPR profile explicitly

The WPR command-line syntax requires a `.wprp!ProfileName[.Verbose]` selector for a custom profile. This command supplies only the `.wprp` path, so it does not explicitly select the PowerToys profile. Add the selector and keep `-filemode`.

```suggestion
wpr -start CPU -start tools\performance\PowerToys.Performance.wprp!PowerToysPerformance.Verbose -filemode
```

confidence.rationale: Microsoft's WPR command-line documentation requires custom profile selection as filename.wprp!ProfileName[.light|.verbose]; the current README supplies no selector. Duplicate base Names are intentional mode variants.

proposed_comments.title: Keep restore traversal inside the PowerToys data tree
proposed_comments.body:
### [P1] Reject restore destinations that cross a reparse-point boundary

**Severity:** `high`

In `tools/performance/Measure-StartupPerformance.ps1`, `Restore-DataFolder` constructs the destination from each snapshotted relative path, creates its parent, and copies with `-Force`, without checking that the destination still resolves inside the PowerToys data tree. If a snapshotted subdirectory is replaced with a junction before restore, this overwrites the corresponding file outside that tree. An isolated reproduction with the exact script reproduced the external sentinel overwrite in both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.

Validate the data root, every destination parent, and any existing destination leaf for reparse points before restoring; reject paths that resolve outside the data root. Use a shared bounded traversal for snapshot/deletion/folder cleanup rather than relying on version-specific recursive enumeration behavior. Recheck a destination immediately before a destructive operation and preserve the backup on any rejected or failed restore.

Verify with a nested snapshotted file whose parent is replaced by a junction to an external sentinel directory: restore must leave the external sentinel unchanged, report the rejected destination, and retain its backup. Ordinary nested files must still restore.

confidence.rationale: All three recursive walks and destination operations are present at the pinned head; combined candidate passed a junction sentinel and restore-path rejection check.

proposed_comments.title: Use the same even-sample median in comparisons
proposed_comments.body:
### [P2] (2/2) Use the same even-sample median in comparisons

**Severity:** `medium`

The comparison script pools the default 10 samples and uses the same lower-middle p50 calculation, so its reported baseline/candidate medians are inconsistent with the conventional median. Average the two middle values for p50 and keep the existing p90 calculation; apply together with (1/2).

```suggestion
    if ($Percentile -eq 0.5 -and $sorted.Count % 2 -eq 0)
    {
        $middle = [int]($sorted.Count / 2)
        return ($sorted[$middle - 1] + $sorted[$middle]) / 2
    }
    $index = [Math]::Max(0, [Math]::Ceiling($Percentile * $sorted.Count) - 1)
```

confidence.rationale: Exact pinned upstream source supports the behavior; the saved candidate and remaining runtime/build limits are stated in the private dossier.
